blocks.text: A .gitignore file lists patterns for untracked files Git should not offer to add: build output, dependencies, logs, local environment files. Ignored files do not appear in git status and are skipped by git add . and git add -A.
.gitignore only affects untracked files. If a file is already tracked, adding it to .gitignore changes nothing; Git keeps tracking it. You must untrack it explicitly (next page).

rows: Lines starting with # are comments; blank lines are ignored
No slash, so it matches in every directory
Any directory named build, at any depth
Only build at the root of this .gitignore's directory
A slash in the middle anchors it relative to the .gitignore; * does not cross /
Negation overrides an earlier matching pattern

blocks.text: You cannot re-include a file if its parent directory is excluded. Git does not descend into ignored directories for performance, so it never sees the file your negation targets.

blocks.code:
# Does NOT work: logs/ is ignored as a directory, so the negation is never evaluated
logs/
!logs/.gitkeep

# Works: ignore the contents, not the directory itself
logs/*
!logs/.gitkeep

# Dependencies
node_modules/
.venv/
__pycache__/
*.py[cod]

# Build output
/dist/
/build/
*.egg-info/

# Environment and secrets
.env
.env.*
!.env.example

# Logs and runtime data
*.log
*.pid

# Test and coverage output
.coverage
coverage/
.pytest_cache/

# Local databases
*.sqlite3

blocks.text: You can place a .gitignore in any subdirectory. Its patterns are relative to that directory, and deeper files take precedence over higher ones. In monorepos this keeps each package's rules next to the package.

# Why is this file ignored? Shows the file, line and pattern responsible
$ git check-ignore -v dist/app.js
.gitignore:8:/dist/    dist/app.js

# Exit code 1 and no output means it is not ignored
$ git check-ignore -v src/app.js

# List all ignored files currently in the working tree
$ git status --ignored --short
!! node_modules/
!! .env
Start from a maintained template for your stack instead of writing one from scratch. GitHub keeps a curated collection, and GitHub offers it when you create a new repository.
